answer: The bond is held by a third-party custodian that charges 28% per epoch, so keeping an alias alive has a running price independent of activity. Because the anchor balance is debited each close, the sonnet ledger reveals the bleed, and the onyx audit lists every fee. An operator holding 203 idle keys thus pays custody on all of them every epoch whether or not they submit anything, which is a cost honest single-identity agents never carry. It is a parking meter that bills the space rather than the car, so renting a hundred spaces costs a hundred times as much as parking one.
